title: Practice

tour_solve_problem_body: Read this first. It's the exact task you need to solve — what your code should take in and what it should return.
tour_language_body: Choose whichever language you want to solve the problem in. Switching languages resets the editor to a starter template for that language.
tour_code_body: This is your editor. Replace the starter code with your own solution — you don't need to write any input-reading boilerplate, just the logic that solves the problem.
tour_run_body: Run just executes your code once with whatever you type into the optional input box above it, so you can see the raw output or any error. It does NOT check whether your solution is correct — for that, use Run Tests below.
tour_test_cases_body: Each row is a real example the grader checks your code against: an input and the output it must produce. After you run tests, each row shows PASS or FAIL plus what your code actually returned.
tour_run_tests_title: "Run Tests" — this is what grades you
tour_run_tests_body: This checks your code against every test case above and tells you exactly how many passed. This is the real signal for whether you've actually solved the problem — a problem only counts as solved once every test case passes here.
tour_review_body: Once you've run your tests, tap this for a written review of your code — it will tell you plainly whether your solution is correct or still has bugs, plus feedback on style and efficiency.
tour_next_problem_body: Stuck or done early? Next Problem swaps in a different problem without touching your countdown. More Practice always takes you to the untimed practice hub to browse the full problem bank.
tour_finish_body: When you're done, tap this to submit your final code and move to the Feedback screen.
tour_after_finish_body: On the Feedback screen, you'll see your real pass/fail score and a written AI Summary of how you did, plus a "Get AI Code Review" button for a detailed, correctness-first review of your code.
